question_text: A developer in eu-west-2 tries to invoke a Claude cross-region inference profile (eu.anthropic.claude-*) for the first time in their account and receives an access error despite having bedrock:InvokeModel permission. What additional IAM permission is required?
explanation: Cross-region inference profiles (eu.* or us.* prefix) require aws-marketplace:Subscribe for the first invocation in an account. bedrock:InvokeModel alone is insufficient. iam:PassRole is for service role delegation, CreateModelInvocationJob is for batch inference, and sts:AssumeRole is for role switching — none resolve this first-use cross-region profile access issue.

question_text: A developer uses a cross-region inference profile ARN (eu.anthropic.claude-*) as the modelId in a RetrieveAndGenerate API call and receives a ValidationException. What is the cause?

options.text: RetrieveAndGenerate only accepts direct foundation model ARNs, not cross-region inference profile IDs
The model is not available in the Region
The Knowledge Base has not synced

explanation: RetrieveAndGenerate validates the model ARN format and rejects cross-region inference profile IDs (eu.* or us.* prefix). You must provide a direct foundation model ARN (arn:aws:bedrock:REGION::foundation-model/MODEL_ID). Model availability issues would be a different error; sync problems affect retrieval not model validation; IAM issues return AccessDeniedException, not ValidationException.
source_topic: RetrieveAndGenerate rejects cross-region inference profile ARN

question_text: A company fine-tunes a foundation model on domain-specific data and notices it now performs significantly worse on general tasks it previously handled well. What is this phenomenon called?
explanation: Catastrophic forgetting occurs when fine-tuning on new data causes the model to lose performance on previously learned tasks — a key reason RAG is preferred over fine-tuning for dynamic knowledge. Data poisoning involves malicious training data; model collapse is losing diversity from synthetic data training; overfitting is poor generalisation within the same domain.
